```{r}
orders <- read.csv("olist_orders_dataset.csv", na = c("","NA"))
order_reviews <- read.csv("olist_order_reviews_dataset.csv", na = c("","NA"))
customers <- read.csv("olist_customers_dataset.csv", na = c("","NA"))
order_items <- read.csv("olist_order_items_dataset.csv", na = c("","NA"))
sellers <- read.csv("olist_sellers_dataset.csv", na = c("","NA"))
products <- read.csv("olist_products_dataset.csv", na = c("","NA"))
product_name_trans <- read.csv("product_category_name_translation.csv", na = c("","NA"))
```

class(orders$order_purchase_timestamp)

Since the dates in the orders data are characters and we need them as dates, we convert them
```{r}
orders <- orders %>%
  mutate(
    order_purchase_timestamp = 
      as.POSIXct(order_purchase_timestamp,
      format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),

    order_approved_at =
      as.POSIXct(order_approved_at,
                 format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    
    order_delivered_carrier_date =
      as.POSIXct(order_delivered_carrier_date,
                 format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    
    order_delivered_customer_date =
      as.POSIXct(order_delivered_customer_date,
                 format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),

    order_estimated_delivery_date =
      as.POSIXct(order_estimated_delivery_date,
                 format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")    
  )
```

```{r}
head(orders)

find missing values

Check by delivery status
```{r}
orders |> 
  filter(is.na(order_delivered_customer_date)) |> 
  count(order_status)
```

Check duplicates and IDs
```{r}
sum(duplicated(orders))
sum(duplicated(order_reviews))
sum(duplicated(customers))
sum(duplicated(order_items))
sum(duplicated(sellers))
sum(duplicated(products))
```
```{r}
orders |> 
  count(order_id) |> 
  filter(n > 1)
```
```{r}
orders |> 
  count(order_id) |> 
  summarise(
    orders = n(),
    duplicated_orders = sum(n > 1)
  )
```
So one row is one order as we expect

Check Customers

```{r}
customers |>

```

```{r}
n_distinct(customers$customer_id)
n_distinct(customers$customer_unique_id)

Meaning that a person can have multiple orders, but most have just one.

Check order items

Check reviews

# Analysis

Check order status and how many orders were delivered

```{r}
orders |> 
  count(order_status) |> 
  mutate(
    percentage = n / sum(n)
  )
```
```{r}
orders |> 
  count(order_status) |> 
  mutate(order_status = fct_reorder(order_status, n)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = order_status, y = n, fill = order_status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = comma(n)),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 4,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "red4"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "mako", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma,    
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Number of orders by order status",
    subtitle = "Sorted from most to least common",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of orders"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", margin = margin(b = 12)),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 20, 15, 15))
```
Check delivery rate

```{r}
orders |> 
  summarise(
    total_orders = n(),
    delivered_orders = sum(order_status == "delivered"),
    non_delivered_orders = sum(order_status != "delivered"),
    delivered_share = mean(order_status == "delivered")
  )
```
Check dates
```{r}
orders |> 
  summarise(
    earliest_purchase = min(order_purchase_timestamp, na.rm = TRUE),
    latest_purchase = max(order_purchase_timestamp, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```
```{r}
orders |> 
  summarise(
    earliest_delivery = min(order_delivered_customer_date, na.rm = TRUE),
    latest_delivery = max(order_delivered_customer_date, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

Check for impossible sequences
```{r}
orders |> 
  filter(
    order_delivered_customer_date < order_purchase_timestamp
  )
```
```{r}
orders |> 
  filter(
    order_delivered_customer_date <
      order_approved_at
  )
```
So a bit weird with these 61 orders that were delivered before they were approved.

Examine the time period
```{r}
orders <- orders |> 
  mutate(
    purchase_month = floor_date(
      order_purchase_timestamp,
      unit = "month"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
orders |> 
  count(purchase_month)
```
```{r}
head(orders)
```
```{r}
orders_monthly <- orders |>  count(purchase_month)
```


```{r}
peak <- orders_monthly %>% filter(n == max(n))

ggplot(orders_monthly, aes(x = purchase_month, y = n)) +
  geom_area(fill = "#2A9D8F", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(color = "#2A9D8F", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "#2A9D8F", size = 2.5) +
  geom_point(data = peak, color = "#E76F51", size = 5) +
  geom_label(
    data = peak,
    aes(label = paste0("Peak: ", comma(n))),
    color = "#E76F51",
    fontface = "bold",
    vjust = -0.8,
    linewidth = 0,
    fill = "white"
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 months", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of orders over time",
    subtitle = "Monthly order volume, with the busiest month highlighted",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of orders"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", margin = margin(b = 12)),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 20, 15, 15)
  )
```

Filtering to have a dataset for the two time spans
```{r}
orders_sep17_sep18 <- orders |>
  filter(
    order_purchase_timestamp >= as.POSIXct("2017-09-01"),
    order_purchase_timestamp <  as.POSIXct("2018-10-01")
  )
```

```{r}
orders_jan17_sep18 <- orders |>
  filter(
    order_purchase_timestamp >= as.POSIXct("2017-01-01"),
    order_purchase_timestamp <  as.POSIXct("2018-10-01")
  )
```

From the two datasets delating the orders without a delivery date
```{r}
delivered_sep17_sep18 <- orders_sep17_sep18 |>
  filter(order_status == "delivered", !is.na(order_delivered_customer_date))

delivered_jan17_sep18 <- orders_jan17_sep18 |>
  filter(order_status == "delivered", !is.na(order_delivered_customer_date))
```


Creating the variables time_to_delivery_days (delivered date - purchase date), delay_days (delivered time-estimated time) and is_late (as a True or False)
```{r}
delivered_sep17_sep18 <- delivered_sep17_sep18 %>% mutate(
      time_to_delivery_days = as.numeric(
        difftime(order_delivered_customer_date,
                 order_purchase_timestamp,
                 units = "days")), 
      delay_days = as.numeric(
        as_date(order_delivered_customer_date) -
          as_date(order_estimated_delivery_date)),
      is_late = delay_days > 0)
delivered_jan17_sep18 <- delivered_jan17_sep18 %>% mutate(
      time_to_delivery_days = as.numeric(
        difftime(order_delivered_customer_date,
                 order_purchase_timestamp,
                 units = "days")),
      delay_days = as.numeric(
        as_date(order_delivered_customer_date) -
          as_date(order_estimated_delivery_date)),
      is_late = delay_days > 0)
```

Analyzing the variables just created
```{r}
delivered_sep17_sep18 |>
  summarise(orders = n(),
            median_time_to_delivery = median(time_to_delivery_days),
            mean_time_to_delivery   = mean(time_to_delivery_days),
            median_delay = median(delay_days),
            late_orders  = sum(is_late),
            late_share   = mean(is_late))

delivered_jan17_sep18 |>
  summarise(orders = n(),
            median_time_to_delivery = median(time_to_delivery_days),
            mean_time_to_delivery   = mean(time_to_delivery_days),
            median_delay = median(delay_days),
            late_orders  = sum(is_late),
            late_share   = mean(is_late))
```
Analyzing delay for sep17_sep18
```{r}
delivered_sep17_sep18 %>% summarise(
    orders = n(),
    mean   = mean(delay_days),
    sd     = sd(delay_days),
    min    = min(delay_days),
    p25    = quantile(delay_days, 0.25),
    median = median(delay_days),
    p75    = quantile(delay_days, 0.75),
    max    = max(delay_days),
    share_early       = mean(delay_days < 0),
    share_on_the_day  = mean(delay_days == 0),
    share_late        = mean(delay_days > 0),
    share_late_over_7 = mean(delay_days > 7),
    median_days_late_of_late_orders = median(delay_days[delay_days > 0])
  )
```

```{r}
delay_median <- median(delivered_sep17_sep18$delay_days)
late_share   <- mean(delivered_sep17_sep18$is_late)

ggplot(delivered_sep17_sep18, aes(x = delay_days, fill = is_late)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, boundary = 0.5, alpha = 0.85, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = delay_median, color = "#2A9D8F", linewidth = 1.2) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = delay_median, y = Inf, vjust = 1.5,
    label = paste0("Median: ", delay_median, " days"),
    color = "#2A9D8F", fontface = "bold", fill = "white", linewidth = 0
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = 15, y = Inf, vjust = 1.5,
    label = paste0("Late: ", percent(late_share, accuracy = 0.1)),
    color = "#E76F51", fontface = "bold", fill = "white", linewidth = 0
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#2A9D8F", `TRUE` = "#E76F51")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-60, 40, by = 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-60, 40)) +
  labs(
    title = "Delivery delay compared with the estimated date",
    subtitle = "Sep 2017 – Sep 2018, late orders highlighted (axis cut at -60/+40 days)",
    x = "Delay (days, negative = early)",
    y = "Number of orders"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", margin = margin(b = 12)),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 20, 15, 15)
  )
```


```{r}

```

Creatin the labels for lateness
```{r}
delivered_sep17_sep18 <- delivered_sep17_sep18 %>%
  mutate(
    lateness = cut(
      delay_days,
      breaks = c(-Inf, -8, -4, -1, 0, 3, 7, Inf),
      labels = c("Very early (8+ days)", "Early (4-7 days)", "Slightly early (1-3 days)",
                 "On time", "Slightly late (1-3 days)", "Late (4-7 days)", "Very late (8+ days)")
    )
  )

count(delivered_sep17_sep18, lateness)

delivered_jan17_sep18 <- delivered_jan17_sep18 %>%
  mutate(
    lateness = cut(
      delay_days,
      breaks = c(-Inf, -8, -4, -1, 0, 3, 7, Inf),
      labels = c("Very early (8+ days)", "Early (4-7 days)", "Slightly early (1-3 days)",
                 "On time", "Slightly late (1-3 days)", "Late (4-7 days)", "Very late (8+ days)")
    )
  )

count(delivered_jan17_sep18, lateness)
```

Analyzing time to delivery
```{r}
delivered_sep17_sep18 %>%
  summarise(
    orders = n(),
    mean   = mean(time_to_delivery_days),
    sd     = sd(time_to_delivery_days),
    min    = min(time_to_delivery_days),
    p25    = quantile(time_to_delivery_days, 0.25),
    median = median(time_to_delivery_days),
    p75    = quantile(time_to_delivery_days, 0.75),
    p90    = quantile(time_to_delivery_days, 0.90),
    p95    = quantile(time_to_delivery_days, 0.95),
    max    = max(time_to_delivery_days),
    share_within_7_days  = mean(time_to_delivery_days <= 7),
    share_over_30_days   = mean(time_to_delivery_days > 30)
  )
  
delivered_jan17_sep18 %>%
  summarise(
    orders = n(),
    mean   = mean(time_to_delivery_days),
    sd     = sd(time_to_delivery_days),
    min    = min(time_to_delivery_days),
    p25    = quantile(time_to_delivery_days, 0.25),
    median = median(time_to_delivery_days),
    p75    = quantile(time_to_delivery_days, 0.75),
    p90    = quantile(time_to_delivery_days, 0.90),
    p95    = quantile(time_to_delivery_days, 0.95),
